title: The projection formula of an adjunction
statement:
Let $P\dashv S$ be an adjunction with $S$ strong monoidal that satisfies the projection
formula ([def-sfb-adjunction-has-projection-formula]). Then the projection formula maps
form a projection formula for $P$ relative to $S$ in the sense of
[def-sfb-projection-formula].

proof.text:
Write $u$ for the adjunction unit and omit the superscript $S$ on $\mu$. For $X,X'\in\mathcal C$, $Y,Y'\in\mathcal D$, $a:X'\to X$, $b:Y\to Y'$, and $x:PX\to Y$, write $T(x):X\to SY$ for its adjoint. By the definition of an adjunction, $T$ is a bijection natural in $X,Y$, so
$$T(b\circ x\circ P(a))=S(b)\circ T(x)\circ a,\qquad T(\mathrm{id}_{PX})=u_X.$$
In particular $T(x)=S(x)\circ u_X$. By [def-sfb-adjunction-has-projection-formula], the prescribed map $\pi_{L,M}$ is characterized by
$$T(\pi_{L,M})=H_{L,M}:=\mu_{L,PM}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{SL}\otimes u_M).$$
All $\pi_{L,M}$ are isomorphisms by the assumed projection-formula property. Use these maps and their unique inverses as the isomorphism data.

source.place: Proof, first sentence and transposition setup; unit clause 4

proof.text:
For $f:L\to L'$, the transposes of the two sides of naturality in $L$ are equal:
$$\begin{aligned}
T(\pi_{L',M}\circ P(Sf\otimes\mathrm{id}_M))
&=\mu_{L',PM}\circ(Sf\otimes u_M)\\
&=S(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{PM})\circ\mu_{L,PM}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{SL}\otimes u_M)
=T((f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{PM})\circ\pi_{L,M}).
\end{aligned}$$
The middle equality is the naturality axiom of the tensorator $\mu$ in its first variable, composed with $\mathrm{id}_{SL}\otimes u_M$. Injectivity of $T$ gives the required equality.

For $g:M\to M'$, naturality of $u$ says $u_{M'}\circ g=SP(g)\circ u_M$. Therefore
$$\begin{aligned}
T(\pi_{L,M'}\circ P(\mathrm{id}_{SL}\otimes g))
&=\mu_{L,PM'}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{SL}\otimes(u_{M'}\circ g))\\
&=S(\mathrm{id}_L\otimes P(g))\circ\mu_{L,PM}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{SL}\otimes u_M)
=T((\mathrm{id}_L\otimes P(g))\circ\pi_{L,M}).
\end{aligned}$$
Here the second equality substitutes the displayed unit naturality and then the naturality axiom of $\mu$ in its second variable. Injectivity of $T$ proves naturality in $M$.

For the unit condition of [def-sfb-projection-formula], let $\epsilon:S\mathbf1\to\mathbf1$ be the inverse monoidal unit map of $S$ and put $q_M=\lambda_M\circ(\epsilon\otimes\mathrm{id}_M):S\mathbf1\otimes M\to M$. The left unit axiom of the strong monoidal functor, composed with the inverse unit map, is
$$S(\lambda_{PM})\circ\mu_{\mathbf1,PM}
=\lambda_{SPM}\circ(\epsilon\otimes\mathrm{id}_{SPM}).$$
Consequently, by naturality of the left unitor,
$$\begin{aligned}
T(\lambda_{PM}\circ\pi_{\mathbf1,M})
&=\lambda_{SPM}\circ(\epsilon\otimes u_M)\\
&=u_M\circ\lambda_M\circ(\epsilon\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)
=T(P(q_M)).
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is naturality of $T$ applied to $\mathrm{id}_{PM}$ and $q_M$. Thus injectivity gives exactly the required unit condition.

For associativity in [def-sfb-projection-formula], fix $L,L',M$, set $N=SL'\otimes M$ and
$$a=\alpha_{SL,SL',M}\circ(\delta_{L,L'}\otimes\mathrm{id}_M):S(L\otimes L')\otimes M\to SL\otimes N,$$
where $\delta_{L,L'}=\mu_{L,L'}^{-1}$. The transpose of the right-hand composite in that definition is
$$\begin{aligned}
T((\mathrm{id}_L\otimes\pi_{L',M})\circ\pi_{L,N}\circ P(a))
&=S(\mathrm{id}_L\otimes\pi_{L',M})\circ H_{L,N}\circ a\\
&=\mu_{L,L'\otimes PM}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{SL}\otimes H_{L',M})\circ a.
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is tensorator naturality followed by $S(\pi_{L',M})\circ u_N=T(\pi_{L',M})=H_{L',M}$. Thus no compatibility of the unit with tensor products, and no monoidal structure on $P$, has been assumed.

source.place: Proof, associativity compatibility: transpose the right-hand composite

proof.text:
Expand $H_{L',M}$ in the final expression of the preceding step. Naturality of the associator with respect to $u_M$, followed by the associativity axiom of $\mu$, gives the explicit equality
$$\begin{aligned}
&\mu_{L,L'\otimes PM}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{SL}\otimes H_{L',M})\circ a\\
&=\mu_{L,L'\otimes PM}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{SL}\otimes\mu_{L',PM})\circ\alpha_{SL,SL',SPM}\circ(\delta_{L,L'}\otimes u_M)\\
&=S(\alpha_{L,L',PM})\circ\mu_{L\otimes L',PM}\circ(\mu_{L,L'}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{SPM})\circ(\delta_{L,L'}\otimes u_M)\\
&=S(\alpha_{L,L',PM})\circ\mu_{L\otimes L',PM}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{S(L\otimes L')}\otimes u_M)
=T(\alpha_{L,L',PM}\circ\pi_{L\otimes L',M}).
\end{aligned}$$
The last line cancels $\mu_{L,L'}\circ\delta_{L,L'}=\mathrm{id}$ using bifunctoriality of tensor. Injectivity of $T$ now gives the associativity condition with exactly the domains and orientation in [def-sfb-projection-formula].

source.place: Proof, associativity compatibility: tensorator associativity and inverse cancellation

proof.text:
The isomorphisms of step 1, their naturality in steps 2 and 3, and the unit and associativity identities in steps 4 and 6 supply precisely all the data and conditions of [def-sfb-projection-formula]. This defines the projection formula for $P$ relative to $S$. Explicitly, for either naturality square put $A=P(Sf\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)$ and $B=f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{PM}$ (step 2), or $A=P(\mathrm{id}_{SL}\otimes g)$ and $B=\mathrm{id}_L\otimes P(g)$ (step 3). The equality $\pi'\circ A=B\circ\pi$ gives
$$A\circ\pi^{-1}=\pi'^{-1}\circ\pi'\circ A\circ\pi^{-1}=\pi'^{-1}\circ B\circ\pi\circ\pi^{-1}=\pi'^{-1}\circ B,$$
which is inverse naturality in each variable.
